proposals.impact: reduce intro drop-off, lift completion rate from 25%
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, 2 of 4 quiz sessions stalled at intro_load and never reached Q1. Only 1 person completed the quiz (25% completion rate). The furthest_step_distribution shows the bleed is happening before any question is answered, which means the problem is the intro screen itself: the framing, the load state, or the opening ask. With traffic coming almost entirely from Instagram (2 of 4 sessions), these are cold visitors who arrived via a short-form post and hit an unfamiliar screen with no established trust. The intro copy is doing the job of a first handshake and it is failing it.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and subheadline. The current text (see CURRENT_TEXT) almost certainly leads with a benefit promise or a question about the visitor's "money type" in language that could belong to any financial personality quiz on the internet. The replacement should name the actual tension the ICP is carrying: earning well, spending it, not knowing where it goes. It should feel like Joel wrote it about a specific Tuesday, not like a quiz product page. One sentence does the job of earning the next click. Keep the CTA button text short and first-person. No structural changes to the component, only the two text nodes.
proposals.current_text:
Discover Your Money Personality

Take our 2-minute quiz to uncover the hidden beliefs driving your financial decisions.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does money still feel like a problem?

This 8-question quiz identifies the specific thinking pattern that keeps capable people spending up to their income, avoiding their accounts, and feeling quietly stuck. Joel built it from his MSc Behavioural Economics research and his own years of doing exactly that.

proposals.impact: lift open rate ceiling already at 50%, test subject line on highest-performing automation
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has the highest open rate of the three active sequences at 50%, with 8 sends and 4 opens. Money Avoidance and Money Worship are both at 16 sends with open rates of 43.75% and 37.5% respectively. Vigilance is outperforming on open rate despite fewer total sends, which suggests the subject line and sender context are landing well with that segment. The highest-leverage content move right now is not to fix what is broken but to study what is working: the Vigilance subject line is the best-performing asset in the email stack and it should inform the subject lines for the two underperforming sequences.
proposals.proposal: Add a short editorial note at the top of the Money Vigilance sequence file that records why the subject line is working, written as a reference for when Joel or Fred rewrites the Avoidance and Worship subjects. Separately, append a proposed A/B subject line variant for email 1 of the Vigilance sequence that pushes further into the specific tension that vigilance types carry: the person who checks their account constantly but still cannot make a financial decision. This is a one-file edit to the sequence frontmatter or top-of-file notes block, not a live automation change.

proposals.impact: restore failed workflow so competitive intel resumes flowing
proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest GitHub Actions workflow failed at 11:44 on 19 May. It is the only failed run in a batch of 14. The workflow is named in a way that suggests it pulls competitive or market intelligence on a schedule. A failed digest means Joel is missing context that was designed to inform content and offer decisions. The coaching page was rewritten and repriced in the same commit window (£597 to £997), which makes competitive awareness more consequential right now, not less. The failure needs diagnosing before the next scheduled run fires and silently produces nothing again.
proposals.proposal:
Add a short triage comment block to the workflow file at the point most likely to have caused the failure. Based on the workflow name and common patterns, the most probable failure points are: an expired API key used to fetch external data, a changed upstream URL, or a missing dependency in the runner environment following a recent package change. The edit adds a TODO comment above the relevant step so Joel sees the likely cause when he opens the file, rather than having to read raw logs. This is not a .github/workflows/ file change to the workflow logic itself, it is a comment insertion in the digest configuration or source file that feeds the workflow, which sits outside the blocked path.

Note to Joel: the blocked paths list includes .github/workflows/*, which means Fred cannot edit the workflow YAML directly. The correct next action is for Joel to open the failed run log in GitHub Actions (Actions tab, filter by "Funnel-Hack Digest", click the red run from 11:44 on 19 May) and check the first red step. The most common cause given recent package.json activity is a Node version mismatch or a missing env secret. Fixing it is a single-line change inside the workflow file once the failing step is identified.
